sections.explanation: In y=A sin(ωt+φ)+c, |A| is amplitude, c the centre, and the period is 2π/|ω| when ω≠0. Python/NumPy trig uses radians. An inverse trig function returns a principal value; further angles can solve the same equation on a stated interval. For sinθ=1/2 on [0,2π), the solutions are π/6 and5π/6. Review a supplied erroneous suggestion only after solving independently: sin(60) is not sin60°.

sections.code:
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
t = np.linspace(0, 4, 200)
y = 2 * np.sin(np.pi * t)
plt.plot(t, y)
plt.xlabel("Time / s")
plt.ylabel("Displacement / m")
plt.show()
print(np.sin(np.deg2rad(60)))
